- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.6) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots next period — dampen forecast by 3–8% for the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., >0.15) over 5+ days, model tends to overestimate mean — adjust downward by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment < 0.10 over last 5 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d often exhibits lag: true price moves 1–2 days ahead of model — shift forecast 1–2 days forward (or adjust last 3–5 days to match true trend).
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.2 to -0.4 in 2 days), model fails to adjust — reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
